key_insight: Ceramic performance is controlled by the processing–microstructure–property–performance chain, where bonding, defects, grain size, porosity, and phase stability determine mechanical, thermal, electrical, and biological behavior.
engineering_relevance: Understanding and controlling ceramic processing enables the design of stronger, more reliable, and application-specific materials for structural, electronic, and biomedical systems.
method: Review of atomic bonding, crystal chemistry, defects, and phase stability in ceramics
Comparison of processing routes including sintering, sol–gel, and additive manufacturing
Survey of biomedical ceramics and emerging directions such as nanoceramics, composites, and data-driven design
evidence_signal: The abstract synthesizes literature across processing routes and ceramic classes rather than reporting a single experimental dataset or benchmark.
watch_item: Ceramics remain challenging to manufacture reliably because brittle fracture, porosity, residual stress, and processing heterogeneity can offset property gains.
paper_title: Ceramic Materials: From Atomic Bonding and Processing to Microstructure, Functional Properties, and Biomedical Applications
